newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil plans big drilling for Statfjord.
newsitem.headline: Statoil plans big drilling for Statfjord.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it planned an extensive drilling programme in 1998 on the oilfields in the Statfjord licence.

Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the drilling programme was aimed at developing new reserves and to maintain plateau production from the Statfjord North and Statfjord East satellites for longer than originally planned.
Work will primarily involve drilling new production wells and overhauling existing wells.
Production wells are planned for an oil development northeast of Statfjord to come onstream in 1998. A final choice of development concept will be made in the spring, Statoil said.
Production drilling also is required on the northern flank of the main field, which will start producing from subsea wells tied back to Statfjord C in early 1999.
Statoil said well workovers also were needed to optimise oil production from the Statfjord satellites, while work was underway to boost recovery from the main field.
The recovery factor on Statfjord currently stands at 62 percent.
The company will utilise the Borgland Dolphin rig. Work will take between 30 and 36 months. --Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41
